newsitem.title: USA: Viad says sells tower to Singapore group.
newsitem.headline: Viad says sells tower to Singapore group.

text.p: Viad Corp said on Monday that it had sold the Viad Tower to a U.S. subsidiary of the Goverment of Singapore Investment Corp, a corporation owned by the Singapore government, for $73 million.
Completed in 1991, the 24-story building has about 484,000 square feet of rentable space and is located on the corner of Central Avenue and Palm Lane in the arts district of downtown Phoenix.
"The sale of the tower is part of our contniuing efforts to divest our non-core assets," said Robert Bohannon, president and chief executive of Viad Corp.

"We will utilize proceeds from the sale to pay down debt and make strategic acquisitons in our core service companies, including airline catering, electronic bill payments, and convention contracting and exhibits," he added.
Viad also said that it would lease back the space it currently occupies in the tower as part of the transaction.
GSIC invests in large-scale commercial properties in North America, Europe and Asia.
